question: Should `needed` mode cover Codex app-server native shell/filesystem/MCP/process surfaces by lazily attaching an OpenClaw sandbox, disabling native tools until sandbox exists, or narrowing the public contract to embedded exec only?
rationale: This is a public sandbox boundary and config contract change, so automation should not choose whether Codex-native execution is included in the permanent `needed` security guarantee without maintainer intent.

options.title: Complete Native Fail-Closed Coverage
options.body: Thread tool activation into Codex app-server native execution or disable native tools under `needed` until an OpenClaw sandbox context exists and can fail closed.

options.title: Narrow The Public Contract
options.body: Document and validate `needed` as embedded exec-only for now, with Codex-native and policy extension support tracked separately before users rely on it.

options.title: Pause The Draft
options.body: Keep the PR paused until the broader sandbox security boundary and policy-extension contract are decided.

recommendation.title: Complete Native Fail-Closed Coverage
recommendation.body: Thread tool activation into Codex app-server native execution or disable native tools under `needed` until an OpenClaw sandbox context exists and can fail closed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from sandbox runtime/docs history and prior security-boundary review context.
